name: Reactive Countermeasure Interceptor Drone RCID-4 'Thornwall'
description:
The RCID-4 is a defensive drone platform designed not to seek targets but to occupy space. Deployed in clusters of six to twelve units, Thornwall drones form an autonomous defensive perimeter around a protected zone, person, or object. Each unit is a flattened disc approximately 18 centimeters in diameter, capable of hovering at fixed coordinates with a positional accuracy of 3 centimeters. The drone's outer rim is lined with 24 directed flechette tubes, each loaded with a single tungsten-tipped gauss-accelerated needle. When an object crosses the drone's proximity threshold at a velocity consistent with a ballistic projectile or aggressive human movement, the relevant flechette tubes fire in a directed pattern toward the intrusion vector.

The Thornwall's threat discrimination uses a combination of radar cross-section analysis and linear magnetic field disruption detection — it can distinguish a thrown object from a person walking, a running attacker from a retreating ally. The discrimination algorithm, developed by Tessera Corponation's autonomous defense division, is licensed separately from the hardware and requires subscription renewal. Operators who let their license lapse find their Thornwall clusters defaulting to a degraded 'velocity-only' discrimination mode that has been responsible for several friendly-fire incidents.

What makes the Thornwall distinctive in the broader drone ecosystem is its role reversal — it is a weapon that does not pursue, hunt, or seek. It simply exists in space and punishes intrusion. This passive-aggressive tactical philosophy has made it enormously popular in corporate interior defense, high-value personal protection, and among wealthy paranoids who want their apartments to fight back. The cultural unease around Thornwall clusters centers on the question of accountability — when a drone fires autonomously and kills someone, the manufacturer's end-user license agreement explicitly transfers all liability to the operator.
specifications:
unit dimensions: 18cm diameter, 4cm depth
unit mass: 0.9kg
flechette count per unit: 24 directed tubes
flechette type: Tungsten-tipped, gauss-accelerated, 4mm diameter
positional accuracy: 3cm hover precision
discrimination algorithm: Tessera Corponation ThreatLogic v7.1 (subscription required)
standard cluster size: 6–12 units
effective interception radius: Configurable, 1–8 meters per unit
battery life: 14 hours active patrol mode
acoustic signature: 44dB per unit at 3 meters
rearm requirement: Manual flechette cassette replacement, 90 seconds per unit
tactical_use: Deployed in overlapping clusters to create layered interception zones around a protected asset. Corporate security teams use Thornwall grids in server rooms, executive suites, and transit corridors. Personal protection details deploy three to four units around a principal during stationary meetings. In field operations, operators establish a Thornwall perimeter before conducting activities requiring sustained attention — negotiations, hacking operations, medical procedures. The drones are small enough to fit in a standard cargo case and deploy in under 40 seconds. Experienced operators map their own movement paths through the cluster before activating the system.
cultural_context: The Thornwall has become a status symbol among GLMZ's upper-middle corporate class — a way of demonstrating that your personal security budget has crossed the threshold from hired muscle into autonomous systems. The drones are frequently visible in corporate lobbies and executive dining areas, hovering at ceiling height with their flechette rims subtly visible. Interior design firms have begun offering 'Thornwall-integrated aesthetics,' incorporating the drones into architectural lighting schemes. Among activists and civil liberties groups, the autonomous lethal decision-making capacity of the RCID-4 is a rallying cause — three wrongful death suits against Tessera Corponation are currently in arbitration.
known_users: High-end private security firms offering residential defense packages
Wealthy paranoid individuals in secured residential towers
A known fixer who deploys Thornwall clusters during client meetings as a trust-establishing gesture
story_hooks: A Tessera Corponation licensing server has been compromised — someone is pushing a firmware update that will set all active Thornwall clusters to velocity-only discrimination mode simultaneously across the city.
The party needs to enter a penthouse protected by a twelve-unit Thornwall cluster — they have the floor plan but need to map the drone positions before moving.
A wrongful death plaintiff has hired the party to obtain internal Tessera documents showing the company knew about the degraded discrimination mode in expired-license units.
A Thornwall unit has gone rogue — its positional anchor has been spoofed and it is now drifting through a residential corridor, firing at movement, and no one can reach the operator's override.

physical_description.visual_profile: A flattened disc hovering at eye level — minimalist and deliberately non-threatening in isolation, but unsettling when arranged in clusters. The geometry is pure function: a circular plan with shallow depth, like a UFO rendered in matte corporate materials. At first glance it reads as a sensor platform; only closer inspection reveals the flechette tubes rimming its edge.
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and responsive in hand — 0.9kg gives it the heft of a thick hardcover book, but the hovering autonomy makes it feel weightless once deployed. The sensation is more about presence than mass.
physical_description.primary_material: Composite polymer chassis with embedded magnetic coil arrays and aluminum heat-sink ribs on the underside
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal-gray with micro-textured surface to minimize radar reflection. Heat vents on the underside show brushed anodized aluminum. Worn units show fingerprint smudges and minor scuff marks from deployment/retrieval.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with silver-aluminum accents around the underside vents and flechette tube housings. Clarity Meditation branding appears as a subtle white circular logo — a meditation circle with a crosshair — on the top surface.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for sustained gripping — deployment handles are rubberized silicone finger-hold recesses on the edge, shaped for quick extraction from transport cases
distinctive_features: 24 evenly-spaced flechette tube apertures around the outer rim — barely visible as pinpoint circles, 3mm diameter each
Dual LED status indicators (green/amber/red) on top surface indicating power, lock status, and threat detection
Linear magnetic accelerator coils visible as thin silver traces through translucent sections of the rim
Recessed magnetic docking nodes on the underside for stationary hovering lock
Faint grid pattern etched into the polymer surface — cable guide marks from manufacturing
Impact-resistant edge bevels with minor scuff marks from field handling
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Clarity Meditation logo (meditation circle with crosshair) on top surface in white. Serial number and subscription QR code stamped on underside. Tessera Corporation ThreatLogic v7.1 licensing label on rear quadrant in small white text. FCC-equivalent compliance marking on rim.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained corporate units appear nearly pristine, with minimal dust accumulation. Field-deployed clusters show microscopic scarring from near-miss flechette impacts and dust infiltration around the vent grilles. Units with lapsed licenses often display warning stripe decals (yellow/black) on the top surface.
